EXORBITANT ELECTRICIAN

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose an electrical contractor that exploits desperate clients, taking a gap responding to emergency call outs and slapping clients with crazy bills.

Unique Selling Point:
CLASSIC CARTE BLANCHE
UNDERCOVER BUST
AND A REPEAT OFFENDER THAT's BEEN ON CB in 2010

Summary:
Mark Levy is a repeat offender. We exposed him in 2010. Same MO. Same Guy. New company name.

After sorting out the initial problem, Levy convinces clients there are bigger problems that need urgent repairs and then klaps them with even bigger invoices sometimes 10 times the actual cost.

But Mr Levy is about to be klapped with a sting and a special visit from Devi.


Further information:
HOW TO DO IT
We interview three case studies that have all been overcharged by Mark Levy since September last year. Bring an expert to the one client’s house to review Levy’s workmanship. And then we do a sting and catch him on the job.

WHO ARE WE DEALING WITH
The three clients didn’t contact Mark directly – they went through websites that appear to use subcontractors. Two case studies contact Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises, another contacted a 24/7 Electrician website. BUT in all the cases the bank account number is the same. It seems like Mark is also not registered with the ECASA and doesn’t seem to have a wireman’s licence.

CASE STUDY 1: JESSICA SWARTZ – ALBERTON

11 November 2019
On Saturday night the Electrical DB Board tripped and in a panic she googled the services of a 24/7 electrical company that could assist at short notice. Jessica came across a company called Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises (http://flashfreezeflush.co.za/).

They assisted by sending through one of their electricians Mark, tel number 076 442 3371, who located the fault and said he needed to replace the earth leakage breaker.

He also said to her that the electrical board is not compliant and that it needs to be rebuilt as the legislation has just changed. She had just moved into the house 6 months prior so could not understand how the COC that she was given was passed the test if what he was saying was true. Levy told her legislation has changed since her initial COC was done – this is untrue. When he finished the work on Saturday evening he charged Jessica R8979 for the work and would not leave until she paid in full. He then returned on Monday to “FIX” the DB board and insert new circuit breakers as he said 10 were missing. He spent just over an hour doing the work and then presented Jessica with a second bill for R31 403 in addition to the R8979. He also would not give her a COC for this and said that would be an additional charge. Once again she was pressured to pay and being a consumer that knows nothing about electrical work she proceeded to pay.

Afterwards she contacted the estate agent to ask about the COC and she referred the invoice - Jessica was given to a number of Electricians who all came back and said the materials used in the invoice cost a max of R3000. Levy charged her 10 times that amount for the work done today.

Freeze Flash Flush refunded her R29 000 for the work done after fighting and threatening them. As they refused to give her a CoC, I arranged for Sovereign Electrical to review the work done and issue me a CoC as I was worried the work they did was illegal.

Jessica moved into her new house on the 31 May 2019 and had a recent CoC which was fully compliant as per the electrician from Sovereign Electrical’s assessment. There was no need for the DB board to be rebuilt as confirmed by both electricians she approached after the incident with Freeze Flash Flush. It was a money marking ploy clearly used by Marc Levy.


CASE STUDY 2: CHEYENN-LEXI COHEN – SANDTON (PROPERY AGENT)
29 September 2019. Cheyenne is a property management agent – one of her clients complained over a weekend in September of electricity tripping at their business premises in Rivonia. She went online and found Flash Freeze Flush who sent out Mark Levy. Apparently there was a problem with the earth leakage – he quoted R 8589 and wanted it paid immediately. Levy insisted there were additional urgent issues that needed fixing and quoted R32000. On Monday the electricity continued tripping – called in a second electrician – the earth leakage switch Levy had installed was too small – this electrician charged only R2000. When she raised it with FFF – they said she should speak to Mark. She insisted on dealing with the company she called, and paid – her mails went unanswered – even after supply a report from the second electrician.

CASE STUDY 3: MATTHEW CHENNELLS – BRUMA
26 November 2019. Sent email to a 24/7 electrical services website – they responded immediately and sent someone out within 30 minutes. Mark Levy walked in and without taking out any screws or anything said it would cost about R12000. Matthew had to go to work, and rushed him for a quoted, he was given a scribbled quote for R12000 – Matthew gave the go ahead and rushed off. The final amount was R14967. Also insisted on payment that day. Matthew had electric problems for a while, he checked briefly by turning on the switches and it worked. After Levy left, Matthew did some more checks and then it all tripped again and smelt like smoke. Called Mark, but battled to get hold of him. He came back and said it was the timing device and removed it – everything switched on and it worked. Afterwards started tripping again. Mark said he’ll come tomorrow, but his promised went on for two weeks and he never showed up. Matthew complained online and blocked Levy on whatsapp. There are still issues.
*WE CAN HAVE AN EXPERT CHECK THE INSTALLATION AND COMMENT ON THE QUOTE.

THE STING:
Set up house with a small electrical problem:

We’ll have an above board electrical expert from Electrical Contractors Association of South Africa that will help us create the fault and give us an estimate of what kind of charges we’re looking at. We’ll rig the house with a camera. When then call in Mark. While he’s busy and given us the quote, Devi and crew will confront him.


EXPERTS:
We'll interview the Electrical Contractors Association of South Africa.
• we’ll use them to help set up the sting – to show us what the problem is and how much it should cost to fix it.
• we’ll get general advice from the Association for consumers that are looking to employ an electrician – what to look out for – what to ask for
• and then also advice for consumers who have been scammed

Script:


VO: Electricity is essential in modern times. It’s more than just having the lights on, it gives us the convenience of appliances that simplify our lives, access to information and the pleasure of entertainment at the click of a button.

LINK: But what happens when the lights go out and it’s not Eskom flipping the switch and plunging you into darkness? You turn what you think are professionals because you shouldn’t take chances with electricity.

VO: Last November, Jessica Swart walked into darkness one Saturday evening. She needed an electrician. She found Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises online. Within half an hour, technician Mark Levy was at her door.

JESSICA: We went through all the different plug points in the house – the rainbird sensor which is the irrigation was struck by lighting and that caused the actual earth leakage to trip.

VO: The bill was R8 979 for less than an hour’s work.

Cheyenne Cohen is a property management agent. In September last year , a business tenant’s electricity kept tripping on a Saturday interrupting services. She also called Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises and Mark arrived.

CHEYENNE: I was kind of caught between a rock and a hard place where I just kind of was. Yes please do what you need to do.

VO: The bill came to R8589 – also for an earth leakage replacement.

This kind of job over a weekend should cost between two and four thousand Rand at a push .

JESSICA: // I thought the earth leakage was the biggest part of the DB board that’s what it cost – I’ve got no clue as a normal consumer.

VO: Jessica & Cheyenne got ripped off by a repeat Carte Blanche offender. This is Mark Levy. We exposed him in 2010 – back then he was also accused of overcharging clients and replacing parts that weren’t broken.

UPSOUND 2010 CB INSERT
MARK: 'this stuff here is all burnt off here. There's no other way i can fix this thing - there's just too much damage in this board.'

VO: And it seems Mark is still pulling the same dodgy moves on unsuspecting clients .

CHEYENNE: He comes up with this whole long story that it's not balanced and that there's an issue with their meter and all this other stuff./that was going to be between the figure of 25 to 30 thousand rand

VO: Cheyenne only approved the initial emergency job. But when the electricity kept tripping the following week, she opted to get a second opinion.

CHEYENNE: The earth leakage installed. He informed he was too small for my board.

VO: There were no issues with the DB Board. The second electrician charged all of R2000 – that’s including, call out, service and the part. R6589 cheaper than Mark’s invoice.

Jessica on the other hand was told her DB board was completely non compliant.

JESSICA: I got a fright because I just moved into this house about six months ago so I couldn't understand why it's not compliant.

VO: But convinced by Mark’s scare tactics - Jessica gave him the go ahead – the bill this time was a shocking R31403.

CHRIS: that is absolutely a blatant fraud in my eyes stealing people's money that.

VO: Chris Koen, is from the Electrical Contractors Association – a voluntary industry regulatory body. Replacing a DB Board for a 3-bedroom house should cost between 4 & 1/2 and R6000 .

CHRIS: I can wire small house, single phase connections, two of them, with that money.

LINK: The consumer protection act is clear….“a supplier must not supply any goods or services at a price that is unfair, unreasonable or unjust.” THESE PRICES ARE Not Fair, REASONABLE Or JUST!

VO: The ECASA recommends no more than a 20% mark up on parts. They worked out the cost prices on Mark’s invoices.

Mark charged a whopping R11589 for Circuit Breakers
The actual cost per unit is no more than 45 rand. That's a mark-up of just over a 2100%.

He also managed to charge Jessica R4895 for an Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker that costs only R363 – that’s a 1300% mark-up – and wait for it – he charged for two of these!

We decided to put Mark Levy to the test again. Mathys de Jager is a qualified, registered Master Electrician with 25 years experience. He created an electrical fault in a home we rigged with hidden cameras.

DEVI: So what exactly have we done.
MATHYS: I've put on a earth fault. On a plug socket where we connect the neutral to the earth. And that that makes the earth leakage trip.

VO: This means the electricity throughout the house will be off, and won’t come back on until that particular plug socket is either disconnected or fixed.

For a job like this, at weekend rates – Mathys would charge R1351 – it shouldn’t cost more than R2500.

DEVI: Could he say he needs to charge us for any kind of parts
MATHYS: To repair the fault. NO, he doesn't have to install any, any material switches or anything

VO: We called out Mark, to get his so-called expert opinion. Within in one minute of arriving - he had a diagnosis.

MARK: Even with the earth leakage and the mains off – your earth leakage is gone

VO: LIE NUMBER 1: That’s not true at all. It seems Mark’s kicked off his assessment with a fabricated fault.

MATHYS: I checked it. There is leakage is working perfectly. He cannot tell you by testing with that tester that this is the Earth leakage is gone. This is just a multi-meter

VO: After fiddling with the DB board for a few minutes, Mark found another fake fault.

MARK: Your neutral bar is cooked.

VO: That’s LIE NUMBER 2….No Mark, it’s actually not cooked at all.

MATHYS: They are all fastened and in tact - so there's nothing wrong with any neutral bar or earth bar.

VO: And then he hit us with the costing…

MARK: Allright. If your earth leakage is gone – you’re gonna look at about R6500

LINK: Mark’s just given us his quote, he’s overpriced – he’s taking chances again….

DEVI: Hi Devi Carte Blanche - You remember me from 10. Years ago.
MARK: that’s a while back ago
DEVI: Do you have your license and registration?
MARK: Not with me
DEVI: we’ve looked I couldn't find you
MARk You need to look for it harder.

VO: We did look extensively; Mark Levy doesn’t appear to have a valid registration with the Department of Labour in terms of the Occupational Health & Safety Act and the Electrical Installation Regulations. He is also not registered with any industry bodies.

CHRIS: He’s operating illegal in my opinion.
DEVI: Does he have to be registered?
CHRIS: Yeah. No that's the law. He does contracting with his contracting work. By law you have to.

VO: Mark never sent us proof of his registration; instead he blocked us on Whatsapp.

DEVI: It's clear that your prices are inflated.
MARK: I give a service. I give a price. The person who's entitled to say yes or no.
DEVI: Except, We are talking inflated prices.
MARK: No, no, no…Tell me why a doctor is entitled to charge you more than the electrician can.
DEVI: So you are like a doctor?
MARK: I charge a service like any other.
DEVI: A supplier must supply
MARK: your interview is over….

VO: He refused to answer questions about the job at hand, Jessica or Cheyenne’s cases. Mark headed for the door.

DEVI: I'm just going to follow you. I'm just going to follow you…..

VO: Bizarrely he was holding the door shut.

DEVI: Why are you doing that?
MARK: Because I don't want you. To fucking open the door. OK. I don't need you to fucking stick a camera up my ass OK?
DEVI: but I'm asking you legitimate questions.
MARK: Fuck You man
DEVI: But I’m asking you legitimate questions.

MARK: Bring that camera to me and I’ll break that fucking camera…
DEVI: No don’t do that….

VO: After trying to intimidate the cameraman, the producer

MARK: What are you going to do?

VO: And eventually me - he stormed off in a rage.

MARK: Now I am after your blood.
DEVI: so you just go around threatening people
MARK: Watch me
DEVI: No I'm watching you, the whole country is watching you

VO: With Mark uncooperative, we turned to Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises – there are a number of websites and Internet posts linked to the company.

LINK: We’ve managed to trace Flash Freeze Flush to this address in Nigel , there are lots of cars in the drive way, but no one seems interested in talking to us.

VO: We eventually heard from the owner Markus Grobler via whatsapp – he declined an on-camera interview and chose to respond in writing through his lawyers. While they didn’t provide any proof of registration for the company or the electricians they use, they stated that Mark Levy was a sub-contractor, who’s services wouldn’t be used until they investigated the allegations.

The company is well aware of Mark Levy’s actions - Jessica complained to them when she established he blatantly lied to her about supposedly new legislation that rendered her DB Board non-compliant.

CHRIS: It was not necessary to put all those circuit breakers in there. He generated work there.

VO: So Jessica paid R31403 for work that wasn’t needed at all - the Legislation last changed in 2009, and the wiring code regulations were last updated in 2017 . Flash Freeze Flush eventually refunded her R29000, when she threatened them with Carte Blanche.

The ECASA recommends getting more than one quote, and using contractors that is registered with the Department and an industry body – it will save you money in the long run.

A lesson Jessica has learnt.

JESSICA: You know I was forty one thousand rent short in my bank accounts // rather just lose your all of the contents of your fridge. How much is it the cost you to replace it?


 
PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Caught red-handed – an electrician tries to dupe his customers into paying thousands of rands for services that sometimes only cost a fraction of the price or even worse aren’t necessary.

PROMO 2
VO: We track down an unscrupulous electrician who’s still duping his clients a decade after being caught on camera - making up faults and grossly overcharging.

PROMO 3
VO: We expose an electrical contractor who exploits desperate clients, taking a gap when responding to emergency call outs and slapping clients with exorbitant bills.

Williams (ASCAP: 199021458, 25%), Jeffrey S Lippencott (ASCAP: 128482662, 25%) ADD7 TX Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 19 January 2020 - Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 03 February 2020 Script: VO: Electricity is essential in modern times. It’s more than just having the lights on, it gives us the convenience of appliances that simplify our lives, access to information and the pleasure of entertainment at the click of a button. LINK: But what happens when the lights go out and it’s not Eskom flipping the switch and plunging you into darkness? You turn what you think are professionals because you shouldn’t take chances with electricity. VO: Last November, Jessica Swart walked into darkness one Saturday evening. She needed an electrician. She found Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises online. Within half an hour, technician Mark Levy was at her door. JESSICA: We went through all the different plug points in the house – the rainbird sensor which is the irrigation was struck by lighting and that caused the actual earth leakage to trip. VO: The bill was R8 979 for less than an hour’s work. Cheyenne Cohen is a property management agent. In September last year , a business tenant’s electricity kept tripping on a Saturday interrupting services. She also called Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises and Mark arrived. CHEYENNE: I was kind of caught between a rock and a hard place where I just kind of was. Yes please do what you need to do. VO: The bill came to R8589 – also for an earth leakage replacement. This kind of job over a weekend should cost between two and four thousand Rand at a push . JESSICA: // I thought the earth leakage was the biggest part of the DB board that’s what it cost – I’ve got no clue as a normal consumer. VO: Jessica & Cheyenne got ripped off by a repeat Carte Blanche offender. This is Mark Levy. We exposed him in 2010 – back then he was also accused of overcharging clients and replacing parts that weren’t broken. UPSOUND 2010 CB INSERT MARK: 'this stuff here is all burnt off here. There's no other way i can fix this thing - there's just too much damage in this board.' VO: And it seems Mark is still pulling the same dodgy moves on unsuspecting clients . CHEYENNE: He comes up with this whole long story that it's not balanced and that there's an issue with their meter and all this other stuff./that was going to be between the figure of 25 to 30 thousand rand VO: Cheyenne only approved the initial emergency job. But when the electricity kept tripping the following week, she opted to get a second opinion. CHEYENNE: The earth leakage installed. He informed he was too small for my board. VO: There were no issues with the DB Board. The second electrician charged all of R2000 – that’s including, call out, service and the part. R6589 cheaper than Mark’s invoice. Jessica on the other hand was told her DB board was completely non compliant. JESSICA: I got a fright because I just moved into this house about six months ago so I couldn't understand why it's not compliant. VO: But convinced by Mark’s scare tactics - Jessica gave him the go ahead – the bill this time was a shocking R31403. CHRIS: that is absolutely a blatant fraud in my eyes stealing people's money that. VO: Chris Koen, is from the Electrical Contractors Association – a voluntary industry regulatory body. Replacing a DB Board for a 3-bedroom house should cost between 4 & 1/2 and R6000 . CHRIS: I can wire small house, single phase connections, two of them, with that money. LINK: The consumer protection act is clear….“a supplier must not supply any goods or services at a price that is unfair, unreasonable or unjust.” THESE PRICES ARE Not Fair, REASONABLE Or JUST! VO: The ECASA recommends no more than a 20% mark up on parts. They worked out the cost prices on Mark’s invoices. Mark charged a whopping R11589 for Circuit Breakers The actual cost per unit is no more than 45 rand. That's a mark-up of just over a 2100%. He also managed to charge Jessica R4895 for an Earth Leakage Circuit Breaker that costs only R363 – that’s a 1300% mark-up – and wait for it – he charged for two of these! We decided to put Mark Levy to the test again. Mathys de Jager is a qualified, registered Master Electrician with 25 years experience. He created an electrical fault in a home we rigged with hidden cameras. DEVI: So what exactly have we done. MATHYS: I've put on a earth fault. On a plug socket where we connect the neutral to the earth. And that that makes the earth leakage trip. VO: This means the electricity throughout the house will be off, and won’t come back on until that particular plug socket is either disconnected or fixed. For a job like this, at weekend rates – Mathys would charge R1351 – it shouldn’t cost more than R2500. DEVI: Could he say he needs to charge us for any kind of parts MATHYS: To repair the fault. NO, he doesn't have to install any, any material switches or anything VO: We called out Mark, to get his so-called expert opinion. Within in one minute of arriving - he had a diagnosis. MARK: Even with the earth leakage and the mains off – your earth leakage is gone VO: LIE NUMBER 1: That’s not true at all. It seems Mark’s kicked off his assessment with a fabricated fault. MATHYS: I checked it. There is leakage is working perfectly. He cannot tell you by testing with that tester that this is the Earth leakage is gone. This is just a multi-meter VO: After fiddling with the DB board for a few minutes, Mark found another fake fault. MARK: Your neutral bar is cooked. VO: That’s LIE NUMBER 2….No Mark, it’s actually not cooked at all. MATHYS: They are all fastened and in tact - so there's nothing wrong with any neutral bar or earth bar. VO: And then he hit us with the costing… MARK: Allright. If your earth leakage is gone – you’re gonna look at about R6500 LINK: Mark’s just given us his quote, he’s overpriced – he’s taking chances again…. DEVI: Hi Devi Carte Blanche - You remember me from 10. Years ago. MARK: that’s a while back ago DEVI: Do you have your license and registration? MARK: Not with me DEVI: we’ve looked I couldn't find you MARk You need to look for it harder. VO: We did look extensively; Mark Levy doesn’t appear to have a valid registration with the Department of Labour in terms of the Occupational Health & Safety Act and the Electrical Installation Regulations. He is also not registered with any industry bodies. CHRIS: He’s operating illegal in my opinion. DEVI: Does he have to be registered? CHRIS: Yeah. No that's the law. He does contracting with his contracting work. By law you have to. VO: Mark never sent us proof of his registration; instead he blocked us on Whatsapp. DEVI: It's clear that your prices are inflated. MARK: I give a service. I give a price. The person who's entitled to say yes or no. DEVI: Except, We are talking inflated prices. MARK: No, no, no…Tell me why a doctor is entitled to charge you more than the electrician can. DEVI: So you are like a doctor? MARK: I charge a service like any other. DEVI: A supplier must supply MARK: your interview is over…. VO: He refused to answer questions about the job at hand, Jessica or Cheyenne’s cases. Mark headed for the door. DEVI: I'm just going to follow you. I'm just going to follow you….. VO: Bizarrely he was holding the door shut. DEVI: Why are you doing that? MARK: Because I don't want you. To fucking open the door. OK. I don't need you to fucking stick a camera up my ass OK? DEVI: but I'm asking you legitimate questions. MARK: Fuck You man DEVI: But I’m asking you legitimate questions. MARK: Bring that camera to me and I’ll break that fucking camera… DEVI: No don’t do that…. VO: After trying to intimidate the cameraman, the producer MARK: What are you going to do? VO: And eventually me - he stormed off in a rage. MARK: Now I am after your blood. DEVI: so you just go around threatening people MARK: Watch me DEVI: No I'm watching you, the whole country is watching you VO: With Mark uncooperative, we turned to Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises – there are a number of websites and Internet posts linked to the company. LINK: We’ve managed to trace Flash Freeze Flush to this address in Nigel , there are lots of cars in the drive way, but no one seems interested in talking to us. VO: We eventually heard from the owner Markus Grobler via whatsapp – he declined an on-camera interview and chose to respond in writing through his lawyers. While they didn’t provide any proof of registration for the company or the electricians they use, they stated that Mark Levy was a sub-contractor, who’s services wouldn’t be used until they investigated the allegations. The company is well aware of Mark Levy’s actions - Jessica complained to them when she established he blatantly lied to her about supposedly new legislation that rendered her DB Board non-compliant. CHRIS: It was not necessary to put all those circuit breakers in there. He generated work there. VO: So Jessica paid R31403 for work that wasn’t needed at all - the Legislation last changed in 2009, and the wiring code regulations were last updated in 2017 . Flash Freeze Flush eventually refunded her R29000, when she threatened them with Carte Blanche. The ECASA recommends getting more than one quote, and using contractors that is registered with the Department and an industry body – it will save you money in the long run. A lesson Jessica has learnt. JESSICA: You know I was forty one thousand rent short in my bank accounts // rather just lose your all of the contents of your fridge. How much is it the cost you to replace it? metadata.Summary: Mark Levy is a repeat offender. We exposed him in 2010. Same MO. Same Guy. New company name. After sorting out the initial problem, Levy convinces clients there are bigger problems that need urgent repairs and then klaps them with even bigger invoices sometimes 10 times the actual cost. But Mr Levy is about to be klapped with a sting and a special visit from Devi.
metadata.Further information: HOW TO DO IT We interview three case studies that have all been overcharged by Mark Levy since September last year. Bring an expert to the one client’s house to review Levy’s workmanship. And then we do a sting and catch him on the job. WHO ARE WE DEALING WITH The three clients didn’t contact Mark directly – they went through websites that appear to use subcontractors. Two case studies contact Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises, another contacted a 24/7 Electrician website. BUT in all the cases the bank account number is the same. It seems like Mark is also not registered with the ECASA and doesn’t seem to have a wireman’s licence. CASE STUDY 1: JESSICA SWARTZ – ALBERTON 11 November 2019 On Saturday night the Electrical DB Board tripped and in a panic she googled the services of a 24/7 electrical company that could assist at short notice. Jessica came across a company called Flash Freeze Flush Enterprises (http://flashfreezeflush.co.za/). They assisted by sending through one of their electricians Mark, tel number 076 442 3371, who located the fault and said he needed to replace the earth leakage breaker. He also said to her that the electrical board is not compliant and that it needs to be rebuilt as the legislation has just changed. She had just moved into the house 6 months prior so could not understand how the COC that she was given was passed the test if what he was saying was true. Levy told her legislation has changed since her initial COC was done – this is untrue. When he finished the work on Saturday evening he charged Jessica R8979 for the work and would not leave until she paid in full. He then returned on Monday to “FIX” the DB board and insert new circuit breakers as he said 10 were missing. He spent just over an hour doing the work and then presented Jessica with a second bill for R31 403 in addition to the R8979. He also would not give her a COC for this and said that would be an additional charge. Once again she was pressured to pay and being a consumer that knows nothing about electrical work she proceeded to pay. Afterwards she contacted the estate agent to ask about the COC and she referred the invoice - Jessica was given to a number of Electricians who all came back and said the materials used in the invoice cost a max of R3000. Levy charged her 10 times that amount for the work done today. Freeze Flash Flush refunded her R29 000 for the work done after fighting and threatening them. As they refused to give her a CoC, I arranged for Sovereign Electrical to review the work done and issue me a CoC as I was worried the work they did was illegal. Jessica moved into her new house on the 31 May 2019 and had a recent CoC which was fully compliant as per the electrician from Sovereign Electrical’s assessment. There was no need for the DB board to be rebuilt as confirmed by both electricians she approached after the incident with Freeze Flash Flush. It was a money marking ploy clearly used by Marc Levy. CASE STUDY 2: CHEYENN-LEXI COHEN – SANDTON (PROPERY AGENT) 29 September 2019. Cheyenne is a property management agent – one of her clients complained over a weekend in September of electricity tripping at their business premises in Rivonia. She went online and found Flash Freeze Flush who sent out Mark Levy. Apparently there was a problem with the earth leakage – he quoted R 8589 and wanted it paid immediately. Levy insisted there were additional urgent issues that needed fixing and quoted R32000. On Monday the electricity continued tripping – called in a second electrician – the earth leakage switch Levy had installed was too small – this electrician charged only R2000. When she raised it with FFF – they said she should speak to Mark. She insisted on dealing with the company she called, and paid – her mails went unanswered – even after supply a report from the second electrician. CASE STUDY 3: MATTHEW CHENNELLS – BRUMA 26 November 2019. Sent email to a 24/7 electrical services website – they responded immediately and sent someone out within 30 minutes. Mark Levy walked in and without taking out any screws or anything said it would cost about R12000. Matthew had to go to work, and rushed him for a quoted, he was given a scribbled quote for R12000 – Matthew gave the go ahead and rushed off. The final amount was R14967. Also insisted on payment that day. Matthew had electric problems for a while, he checked briefly by turning on the switches and it worked. After Levy left, Matthew did some more checks and then it all tripped again and smelt like smoke. Called Mark, but battled to get hold of him. He came back and said it was the timing device and removed it – everything switched on and it worked. Afterwards started tripping again. Mark said he’ll come tomorrow, but his promised went on for two weeks and he never showed up. Matthew complained online and blocked Levy on whatsapp. There are still issues. *WE CAN HAVE AN EXPERT CHECK THE INSTALLATION AND COMMENT ON THE QUOTE. THE STING: Set up house with a small electrical problem: We’ll have an above board electrical expert from Electrical Contractors Association of South Africa that will help us create the fault and give us an estimate of what kind of charges we’re looking at. We’ll rig the house with a camera. When then call in Mark. While he’s busy and given us the quote, Devi and crew will confront him. EXPERTS: We'll interview the Electrical Contractors Association of South Africa. • we’ll use them to help set up the sting – to show us what the problem is and how much it should cost to fix it. • we’ll get general advice from the Association for consumers that are looking to employ an electrician – what to look out for – what to ask for • and then also advice for consumers who have been scammed
